note: What lanekit is, for the lane tooling: lanekit gives itself lanes, so its own work goes the way it
WHICH LANEKIT RUNS. The shim looks for lanekit at ../lanekit before ~/.lanekit, and beside a lane
of this repository that is this main checkout. So lane commands (new, gate, land, sweep, web)
always run main's lanekit, never a lane's half-made one. A lane's own code is what its gate
tests (./check runs node --test in the lane) and what runHint serves: the page from the lane's
dev/, on the lane's port. To try a lane's commands by hand, run node <lane>/dev/lane.mjs.
Nothing to copy, link or seed: lanekit has no dependencies, no environment file and no database,
and its tests make their own scratch repositories. Every change earns tier 1, all the tests.
name: lanekit
